generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and sport science, the plan runs from first session to final answer. You might revise a training principle actively by walking through its stages, mix flashcards on muscle groups with explaining a study aloud, and test yourself on key terms. Then you carry that control into the exam, pacing a question on, say, energy systems to the clock. The strands work as one approach, not three.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport students revised energy systems for the same exam. One read the notes over, used one technique, and made no plan for the day, then ran short of time. The other built flashcards, explained the systems aloud, walked through the stages to fix the sequence, and sat the exam to a timed plan. His preparation held together, and his marks improved.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and sport science, active revision works best as one connected plan. You let active learning guide a varied mix of techniques, run it across your programme, and carry that control into a timed exam. The joined-up approach, not any single technique, is what turns preparation into marks.

check.body: A student revises a topic actively, uses a mix of techniques across families, and sits the exam to a calm, timed plan. They do better than on earlier exams. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three strands work together: active revision, a varied technique mix and an exam-day plan form one approach.
_items.feedback: Yes. The strands joined up into one plan, and that is what paid off.

_items.text: That only the exam-day plan made the difference to their result.
_items.feedback: The exam-day plan protected marks, but active revision and the technique mix earned them.

_items.text: That they simply spent far more hours than before.
_items.feedback: The point is the joined-up approach, not extra hours.

_items.text: That the techniques alone, without active learning behind them, improved the result.
_items.feedback: The techniques work because active learning is the principle driving them.
